latest_release.body:
## ⚙️ Process Updates

## Go bumped to `v1.27.3` for a security fix

The version of Golang used to compile the Terragrunt binary has been updated from `v1.27.2` to `v1.27.3`.

Go `v1.27.3` is a security release. It fixes [CVE-2026-111943](https://go.dev/issue/82345) in `crypto/x509`: certificate verification now rejects chains that contain a small set of untrusted intermediate certificates. Terragrunt uses this verification for every HTTPS connection it makes, including source downloads, provider registry lookups, and remote state backends. We recommend upgrading.

## Terragrunt runs `git`, `hg`, and `smbclient` source downloads itself

Terragrunt downloaded `git::`, `hg::`, and `smb://` sources through the getters built into the [go-getter](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-getter) library, which started `git`, `hg`, and `smbclient` on their own. Terragrunt now implements these getters itself and starts those programs the same way it runs every other command.

Downloads should behave as they did before. If you find any functional difference, [open an issue](https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/issues).

Because the downloads now go through Terragrunt's own command handling, Terragrunt's tests can cover them without a real `git`, `hg`, or `smbclient` install or a remote server, which makes regressions in source downloads easier to catch.

## 🏎️ Performance Improvements

## Faster parsing of shared configuration

Repositories where every unit includes a `root.hcl` that loads shared files with [`read_terragrunt_config`](https://docs.terragrunt.com/reference/hcl/functions#read_terragrunt_config) now parse much faster.

- Each unit used to parse those shared files itself, so a `common.hcl` that runs `yamldecode(file(...))` on a large YAML file decoded it once per unit. Terragrunt now parses each file once and gives every unit the same result, and parses it again only when the file, or a file it reads, changes during the command. `run --all` parses it a second time when the run starts, after discovering units. A file whose result can differ between units, like one that calls `get_original_terragrunt_dir()` or has `dependency` blocks, is still parsed per unit.
- Since v1.1.2, discovery parsed every included configuration twice, once for its feature flag defaults and once to merge it. It parses each include once again, and skips includes with `merge_strategy = "no_merge"` that it would only have thrown away.
- Locals and inputs went through a JSON encoding round trip on their way into Terragrunt. Terragrunt now converts them directly.

In [benchmarks](https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/blob/main/internal/discovery/benchmark_shared_config_test.go) on an Apple M3 Max, discovering units and their dependencies in a generated repository whose units read a 48 KB YAML file through `read_terragrunt_config`:

| units | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100 | 819ms | 59ms |
| 500 | 3.60s | 201ms |
| 1,000 | 7.01s | 379ms |
| 5,000 | 34.2s | 1.88s |

Memory allocated during discovery dropped by about 95%.

## Faster discovery with path filters

Terragrunt now analyzes `--filter` expressions before discovery starts and uses them to narrow the filesystem walk it does during discovery. Filters that name specific paths let Terragrunt skip most of the walk, or walk only the directories those paths can match.

On a repository of 10,000 units, discovery with a filter like `--filter './doublestar/glob/**'`, matching 1,250 of those units, took 27 ms instead of 224 ms. A filter like `--filter './path/to/specific/unit'`, which names a single unit, took under 1 ms instead of 215 ms. Discovery selects the same units as before. It still walks the whole working directory when there is no filter, when every filter is negated, or when any filter can select a unit anywhere, such as `name=vpc` or `...vpc`.

# Terragrunt

[![Maintained by Gruntwork.io](https://img.shields.io/badge/maintained%20by-gruntwork.io-%235849a6.svg)](https://gruntwork.io/?ref=repo_terragrunt)
[![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt)
[![GoDoc](https://godoc.org/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt?status.svg)](https://godoc.org/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt)
![OpenTofu Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/tofu-%3E%3D1.6.0-blue.svg)
![Terraform Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/tf-%3E%3D0.12.0-blue.svg)

Terragrunt is a flexible orchestration tool that allows Infrastructure as Code written in [OpenTofu](https://opentofu.org)/[Terraform](https://www.terraform.io) to scale.

Please see the following for more info, including install instructions and complete documentation:

* [Terragrunt Website](https://terragrunt.com)
* [Getting started with Terragrunt](https://docs.terragrunt.com/getting-started/quick-start/)
* [Terragrunt Documentation](https://docs.terragrunt.com/)
* [Terragrunt Scale](https://docs.terragrunt.com/terragrunt-scale/)
* [Contributing to Terragrunt](https://docs.terragrunt.com/community/contributing)
* [Commercial Support](https://gruntwork.io/support/)

## Join the Discord!

Join [our community](https://discord.com/invite/YENaT9h8jh) for discussions, support, and contributions:

[![](https://dcbadge.limes.pink/api/server/https://discord.com/invite/YENaT9h8jh)](https://discord.com/invite/YENaT9h8jh)
